why: Signals are a closed set, declared with `export signal <Name>;`. The same code is emitted by all three uses, worded `handler for undeclared signal`, `wait for undeclared signal` and `emit of undeclared signal`, because they are one fact: the name is not in the declared set, so it can only be a typo. A handler for it waits forever, a wait on it blocks until its timeout every time, and an emit of it fires into nothing without reporting anything.
fix: or check the spelling — the name must match a declared signal exactly
